The SEIRV module for the XH component

Source: R/host-xde-SEIRV.R
SEIRV.Rd

Implements the XH component using a Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered-Vaccinated (SEIRV) compartmental model of human infection dynamics, extending SEIR with a vaccinated compartment. This implementation includes human demographic change and support for progressive stratification.

State Variables

H

total human (or host) population density

E

density of exposed (infected but not yet infectious) humans

I

density of infectious humans

R

density of recovered humans

V

density of vaccinated humans

S=H-E-I-R-V

density of susceptible humans or hosts

Dynamical Term

\(h\) or foi

The force of infection is computed and stored by Exposure as FoI

A constant fraction of infectious bites causes an infection: the parameter \(b\).

Parameters

make_XH_obj_SEIRV supplies defaults for all parameters. change_XH_pars.SEIRV currently changes b, c, r, tau, gamma, and q; it leaves alpha and varepsilon unchanged.

q

test positivity (default 0.8)

b

transmission probability from mosquito to human

c

transmission probability from human to mosquito

tau

rate of progression from exposed to infectious

r

clearance rate for infections

alpha

proportion of births that are vaccinated

varepsilon

proportion of recovered individuals that gain vaccine-like protection

gamma

rate of loss of immunity in \(R\)

Infection Dynamics

Exposed individuals become infectious at rate \(\tau\). Infections clear at rate \(r\); a fraction \(\varepsilon\) enter the vaccinated class, while the rest enter the recovered class. Recovered immunity wanes at rate \(\gamma\). A fraction \(\alpha\) of births enter the vaccinated class, which has no waning term. $$ \begin{array}{rl} dE/dt &= hS - \tau E - \mathbf{D}(E) \\ dI/dt &= \tau E - rI - \mathbf{D}(I) \\ dR/dt &= (1-\varepsilon)rI - \gamma R - \mathbf{D}(R) \\ dV/dt &= \alpha\mathbf{B}(t,H) + \varepsilon rI - \mathbf{D}(V) \\ \end{array}$$ where \(h\) is the force of infection. The mortality function uses the same model for each compartment as for \(H\). Susceptible density \(S=H-E-I-R-V\) is redundant and is computed after solving.

Prevalence

F_pr_obs.SEIRV returns observed prevalence \(x_q=qI/H\).

F_prevalence.SEIRV returns \(x=I/H\). In contrast, parse_XH_orbits.SEIRV stores true_pr as \((E+I)/H\). This module has no diagnostic sensitivity parameters or module-specific light microscopy, RDT, or PCR prevalence methods.

Infectiousness

The probability that a mosquito becomes infected after feeding on an infectious host is \(c\). Infectious density is \(cI\), and net infectiousness is \(cI/H\).

Mass Treatment

This implementation does not initialize or use mda(t) or msat(t), and has no treatment parameters rho or sigma.

Demography

This model has no parameters or terms to describe disease-induced mortality.

Births or \(\mathbf{B}\)

the births function

Deaths or \(\mathbf{D}\)

the deaths function

Setup:

The default is a constant population model: birth and death rates are set to zero

  • Use setup_births to configure Births

  • Use setup_deaths to configure Deaths

Also, see xds_info_demographic_change.
